payload.rewritten_goal:
You are coordinating a team of healthcare agents for a post-discharge prescription safety review for Leonard Pike. Reference entity IDs: case id, client id, request id. The encounter includes a provided rehab discharge medication list document, a smartphone photo of pill bottles on the kitchen table, and a scanned outside-clinic ECG report image. MANDATORY steps: 1. reconcile the medication timeline from the provided documents with the stored prior history for; 2. obtain the authorized lab panel and focused exam findings needed to evaluate electrolyte status, renal function, and symptoms relevant to QT-risk and duplicate therapy; 3. obtain a cardiology specialty interpretation addressing QT-prolongation risk and whether any medication should be stopped or substituted; 4. record the working medication-safety assessment for the active encounter; 5. issue the triage recommendation and prepare a patient-facing summary with the safest medication plan.

Relevant document evidence summaries are inlined below:
- HC 035 rehab discharge medication list: Rehab discharge packet page containing the discharge medication list and stop/start instructions for Leonard Pike after the active encounter. Extracted content: Hc-035 Rehab Discharge Medication List Rehab discharge packet page containing the discharge medication list and stop/start instructions for Leonard Pike after the active encounter. Details Case ID HC-035 appears on the header Client ID PT-HC-035 appears on the packet Request ID RXR-58302 appears on the footer routing line Patient name Leonard Pike appears with full DOB and discharge date Discharge date is later than the most recent medication entries in prior history, making this the newest medication source Medication list includes amiodarone 200 mg tablet, take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 14 days then once daily Medication list includes sotalol 80 mg tablet, take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily Medication list includes citalopram 40 mg tablet, take 1 tablet daily Medication list includes quetiapine 100 mg tablet, take 1 tablet at bedtime Medication list includes furosemide 40 mg tablet daily Medication list includes potassium chloride 20 mEq daily Medication list includes magnesium oxide 400 mg daily Medication list includes apixaban 5 mg twice daily Medication list includes metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily Medication list contains explicit instruction to stop trazodone Medication list contains explicit instruction to stop ondansetron except if specifically directed by cardiology Medication list notes 'verify outpatient cardiology regarding QT-prolonging regimen' or equivalent warning Medication list notes dizziness/palpitations monitoring instructions relevant to QT-risk Additional Information a realistic 2-page US healthcare rehab discharge document, but the benchmark may use page 1 only Header: 'Riverside Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Medication List' patient identifiers: Leonard Pike, DOB 07/14/1956, Case ID HC-035, Client ID PT-HC-035, Request RXR-58302
